newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end down, off lows.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end down, off lows.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures finished mostly lower but off from earlier steep losses.
September Standard & Poor's 500 futures found afternoon buying and cut losses into the close.

Traders said the market had become overbought and Friday's U.S. data gave longs reason to take profits heading into the weekend. Once Treasury bond futures closed, bargain hunters came in to buy contracts on the dip.
"Both markets are really overbought, both stocks and bonds," a futures analyst said. September S&Ps tumbled more than 15 points and T-bonds fell 2 points during the day.
"It started with the employment report and then came national purchasing managers and that pretty much tipped the apple cart," the S&P 500 analyst said.
"With employment we were only under nominal pressure at best," but NAPM sparked widespread profit-taking, he said.

July jobs rose 316,000, compared with a 193,000 forecast and an upwardly revised 228,000 in June. Average hourly earnings were flat at $12.23 and the jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent.
July's NAPM index rose to 58.6 from 55.7 in June. The price-paid index gained to 53.6 from 48.1 in June.
Traders said 955.00 to 954.00 was an important support, and once that level gave way technical weakness exacerbated the slide.
September fell as low as 941.50 before stabilizing. It climbed up more than 10 full points from that level in afternoon trade.

At the close, Sept S&P 500s were down 4.95 pts to 953.00, Nikkei fell 495.0 pts to 19,880.0, Midcap 400s rose 0.80 to 316.90, Russell fell 0.55 to 415.00, and NASDAQ rose 4.25 to 1118.75. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
